title: Write your résumé once, export it everywhere

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine updating your résumé in one place, and getting a PDF, a web page and a section of your own website out of it. That's the pitch of JSON Resume, and Antoine wrote a walkthrough.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I usually have three versions of my CV and none of them match. How does it work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's an open schema, maintained by the community. You keep one plain JSON file called resume dot json. Because it's just data, themes and command-line tools can swap the presentation without you touching the content.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what goes in the file?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Predictable blocks. Basics, with your name, headline, email and profiles like LinkedIn and GitHub. Then work, education, skills and projects. Work has the company, title, dates and a short summary. Skills can have a level and a few keyword tags.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And then you turn it into something people can read.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. You install the resume CLI with npm, pick a theme, and run resume export to get HTML or PDF. The sample grid in the post shows themes like Elegant, Paper, Kendall and Flat. You can also publish to the free JSON Resume Registry for a hosted page.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What if you already have a site?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If it runs on Hugo, a module called hugo-mod-json-resume maps the JSON sections into templates, even in several languages. That's how you go from a standalone export to a CV section inside a personal blog. There are also tools to preview while you edit, and one that bootstraps the file from LinkedIn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine's table says it's strong for a developer CV that changes often. For a heavy design portfolio, you'd export the PDF and do the layout elsewhere. And for corporate portals that only take plain text, it still helps you generate that text.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three. Letting the file rot, so set a reminder after each job change. Theme drift across npm versions, so pin the theme in CI. And stuffing in every project, because interviewers skim.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the point is content versus presentation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. One source of truth, themes for layout. The full write-up has the code samples for every section.
